references.text: In [ref:Luk 15:18-19|Luke 15:18-19], the prodigal son plans the words he will say to his father—the same words he actually speaks in verse 21. The comparison shows that the son remains true to his decision to confess his sin.

In [ref:Luk 15:12|Luke 15:12], the son asks for his share of the inheritance and leaves his father, which forms the background for the confession "I have sinned against heaven and before you" in verse 21.
[ref:Sal 51:6|Psalm 51:6] contains David's confession "against you only have I sinned", reflecting the prodigal son's recognition of having sinned against heaven and against his father.
[ref:Sal 51:4-6|Psalm 51:4-6] is David's great confession of sin, where he asks for mercy and acknowledges his sin before God, paralleling the prodigal son's sincere confession to his father.

In [ref:2 Mos 10:16|Exodus 10:16], Pharaoh says "I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you", a formulation similar to the prodigal son's confession of having sinned against heaven and against his father.

In [ref:4 Mos 21:7|Numbers 21:7], the people confess "we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against you". The expression of sinning both against God and against a person parallels Luke 15:21.
In [ref:1 Sam 15:24|1 Samuel 15:24], Saul confesses "I have sinned", a similar confession of sin to what the prodigal son makes before his father.
In [ref:2 Sam 12:13|2 Samuel 12:13], David says "I have sinned against the Lord", a parallel confession where the sinner acknowledges guilt before God, just as the prodigal son does.

In [ref:Luk 18:13|Luke 18:13], the tax collector beats his breast and prays "God, be merciful to me, a sinner!"—a similar humble acknowledgment of unworthiness, paralleling the prodigal son's confession.

In [ref:Luk 5:8|Luke 5:8], Peter says "go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man", an acknowledgment of unworthiness that recalls the prodigal son's words "I am no longer worthy to be called your son".
